analysis.answer: Current law sets the state personal income tax rate at 5 percent of taxable income. This measure increases that rate to 6 percent starting in the 2028 tax year.
The direct cost to taxpayers is an additional 1 percent of their taxable income. This represents an opportunity cost for households, which will have less disposable income for consumption or saving.

Individuals, families, and pass-through businesses subject to the personal income tax bear the cost of the rate increase. The state government, and the populations that rely on state-funded services and programs, benefit from the increased revenue.

Taxpayers may adjust their behavior to minimize tax liability, such as altering investment strategies or timing income realization. Some mobile high-income earners or pass-through businesses may consider relocating to jurisdictions with lower tax rates.

The effect of state income tax rate increases on economic growth and migration is empirically disputed. Some researchers find that tax increases prompt out-migration of high earners and businesses, ultimately dampening job growth and economic output. Other researchers find minimal migration effects and argue that the resulting increased public investment (such as in education or infrastructure) can yield net-positive economic effects.
